brief.subject: FBI flags midterm election scams; FTC sends Walmart refunds
brief.headline: FBI Warns of Midterm Election Scams as FTC Mails $9.8 Million in Refunds
brief.dek: FBI flags fraud tied to the 2026 midterms, the FTC reports on scams hitting older adults, and wire-transfer victims get refunds.
brief.lede: The FBI says scammers are using the 2026 U.S. midterm election to run multiple fraud schemes. Expect more election-themed calls, texts and emails before November.

sections.heading: Midterm election scams are here
bullets: The FBI warned on Oct. 15 that scammers are exploiting the 2026 midterms with multiple fraud schemes.
A separate FBI alert cautions voters about election crimes ahead of the November vote.
Be skeptical of unexpected political messages, especially ones that pressure you to act fast or send money.

sections.heading: FTC report on fraud against seniors
bullets: The FTC sent Congress its Protecting Older Consumers 2025-2026 report on Oct. 19.
It draws on fraud reports filed by older adults to identify key scam trends.
The report also details FTC enforcement against deceptive practices that target older Americans, useful context for families watching out for parents.

sections.heading: Walmart wire-fraud victims get refunds
bullets: The FTC is sending more than $9.8 million to people scammed through Walmart's wire transfer services.
Regulators say scammers used those services to take hundreds of millions of dollars from U.S. consumers.
Walmart settled FTC charges in June 2025 over allegedly weak anti-fraud policies and staff training.

sections.heading: Ticket broker sued over purchase limits
bullets: The FTC accused broker REPS & Company Inc. of dodging per-event ticket limits to buy millions of tickets.
The company allegedly resold those seats to high-demand events at a significant profit, squeezing fans who pay face value.
The Justice Department filed the complaint after a referral from the FTC.
